bullets.title: NVDA: Vera Rubin platform launches with 10x perf/watt; 1,000 racks/day production report
bullets.body: NVIDIA revealed details on its Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, claiming 10x better performance per watt vs. Blackwell and 10x improvement in tokens/megawatt (per CoreWeave's first measured data on DeepSeek-R1). The Information reports NVDA could manufacture ~1,000 Vera Rubin racks/day, implying a ~$630B quarterly revenue run-rate—the author is skeptical but notes the bull case is real. NVDA also briefed on the Vera CPU (monolithic, not chiplet, Arm-based), positioned for agentic workloads, and claims Vera outperforms AMD's Turin; ecosystem partners CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft, Oracle, SpaceX, and Tesla are standing up deployments. Spectrum-6 (102.4 Tbps ethernet switch) is shipping to these partners now.

bullets.title: AMD: Azure Helios win breaks NVDA rack monopoly; analyst raises PT to $640 on Anthropic deal
bullets.body: AMD secured the Microsoft Azure Helios AI rack contract, described as the first real test of NVDA's data center rack monopoly. Separately, AMD is pricing its Helios rack ~40% above NVDA's second-gen Rubin, betting customers absorb the premium. One analyst raised AMD's PT to $640 (45x 2027E EPS), revised 2027E EPS up 11%, and expects Anthropic to be unveiled as AMD's third GW-scale customer—a deal GFHK expects to exceed Meta and OpenAI in 2027 scale. AMD's Advancing AI event this week is expected to highlight underappreciated CPU demand.

bullets.title: MU: +13% on TSMC price hike catalyst; bullish options flow; short sellers in panic
bullets.body: Micron surged ~13% intraday, largely attributed to reports that TSMC plans to raise foundry/chipmaking prices 5-10% in 2027 (boosting memory pricing power) and SK Hynix CEO warning the memory chip shortage will worsen before improving. AI datacenter DRAM demand is cited as the structural driver. MU showed the most bullish options flow in the market session; short sellers described as having paper profits wiped out.

bullets.title: TSM: Plans 5-10% foundry price hike in 2027; shares fell 7.3% post-earnings on AI model risk
bullets.body: TSMC is reportedly planning a 5-10% price increase for chipmaking services starting in 2027 to offset higher material, equipment, and overseas fab construction costs; increases vary by customer and product. Despite reporting a 77.4% jump in quarterly net income, TSMC's Taiwan-listed shares fell 7.3% the day after earnings—market reaction driven by concern that Kimi K3 (2.8T parameter open model) could reduce chip intensity.

bullets.title: INTC: Data center layoffs planned; EMIB packaging may be bigger AI opportunity than 18A
bullets.body: Intel plans layoffs within its data center group, per an insider, though the scale of cuts is unclear. Separately, analysts argue INTC's EMIB advanced packaging—not 18A process—could be its biggest AI opportunity, with inference dynamics potentially shifting competitive landscape vs. TSM's CoWoS. Intel and Fortinet also announced a strategic collaboration on Fortinet's SP6 security processor.

bullets.title: TSLA: Robotaxi expands to Tampa, Orlando, Florida; unusual $2.1M OTM call activity; earnings tomorrow
bullets.body: Tesla's robotaxi/ride-hailing service is now live in 7 areas including Orlando (unsupervised Model Y) and Tampa/Florida. Ahead of Q2 earnings (tomorrow), one analyst estimates adj. EPS of $0.60 vs. $0.55 consensus, assuming 18.8% auto gross margins ex-credits and 480K deliveries. Unusual $2.1M OTM call activity (10 DTE) detected. Bears note TSLA is down 15% YTD vs. F +9%, GM flat, citing management's pattern of overpromising; Cybertruck 240K/year target remains unmet after 18 months.

bullets.title: AAPL: Launching 'Apple Upgrade' device leasing program July 28 with Klarna
bullets.body: Apple is partnering with Klarna to launch 'Apple Upgrade'—a subscription-based leasing/lease-to-own program—on July 28 in the U.S., covering most iPhone, Mac, iPad, and Apple Watch models. Users can pay off early, upgrade early, or keep devices. The program is designed to accelerate upgrade cycles. AAPL is currently trading at elevated multiples: P/E 40x vs. 10-yr avg of 26x; EV/EBITDA 31x vs. 19x avg.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Launches Gemini 3.6 Flash family; starts Gemini 4 pre-training
bullets.body: Google announced Gemini 3.6 Flash ($1.50/$7.50 per million input/output tokens), Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite ($0.30/$2.50), and Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber. Google is also testing Gemini 3.5 Pro with select partners ahead of broader release and has begun pre-training for Gemini 4. Aggressive pricing signals Google is competing hard in the AI inference market.

bullets.title: MSFT: Using Kimi K3 for Copilot (potential 60% token cost savings); expands Mistral partnership
bullets.body: Reports indicate Microsoft will use Kimi K3 (Moonshot AI's 2.8T parameter model) to power flagship Copilot, potentially saving 60% per token. Separately, Microsoft and Mistral AI announced a multibillion-dollar expanded partnership integrating Mistral models across Azure, Copilot Studio, and Microsoft Foundry, with Mistral adding GPU capacity.

bullets.title: NVDA/IREN/HUT: Nvidia stakes multibillion-dollar AI cloud deals with Hut 8 and IREN
bullets.body: NVIDIA has locked multibillion-dollar AI cloud infrastructure partnerships with Hut 8 and IREN, and also staked Nebius. IREN currently has more announced projects under review than NBIS. These deals reinforce NVDA's strategy of anchoring GPU compute buildout through direct investments in cloud/data center operators.

bullets.title: NBIS: 50%+ of 2026 ARR to come from enterprises/AI labs; hyperscaler dependency a stop-gap
bullets.body: Nebius (NBIS) has acknowledged that selling compute to hyperscalers is a transitional business; management targets 50%+ of 2026 ARR from enterprises, AI labs, and non-hyperscaler customers, who represent longer-term relationships. IREN currently has more announced pipeline under review than NBIS.

bullets.title: HOOD: Needham raises PT to $123; stock +8% as super-app thesis strengthens
bullets.body: Needham raised its Robinhood price target to $123, citing continued strength in equities, options, prediction markets, and crypto. The firm sees HOOD as a leading contender to become a financial super app. StockTwits founder Howard Lindzon's early investment (at $8M valuation) highlighted as credibility signal.

bullets.title: DIS: ESPN conducting fresh layoffs tied to NFL Network integration
bullets.body: Disney-owned ESPN is making another round of job cuts, with most layoffs tied to the consolidation of NFL Network operations. Disney also announced a multiyear partnership with Kraft Heinz to serve its products at Disney parks and use Disney characters on retail goods.

bullets.title: AMD MI500X ISA released; MI455X adds TMA-style architecture modeled after NVDA Hopper
bullets.body: AMD released the MI500X ISA, which includes 1 TDM MOE descriptor shared across all experts. The MI455X is adding TDM (RMA) capability, explicitly modeled after NVIDIA's SM90 Hopper TMA architecture—signaling AMD is closing architectural gaps in its GPU stack.

bullets.title: Semi sector rips: SOX +5.5%; AMD +8%, INTC +8%, MU +13%, SNDK +12% lead
bullets.body: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 5.5% as AI chip stocks staged a powerful rebound. Key movers: MU +12.5%, SNDK +12.8%, INTC +8.2%, AMD +8.1%, MRVL +7.3%, LITE +9.3%, TSEM +10.4%. The primary catalyst was the TSMC chipmaking price hike report and AI data center demand narrative. Market shrugged off escalating U.S.-Iran geopolitical tensions.

bullets.title: ARM: Described as most foundational AI play; architecture in every NVDA GPU and AWS Graviton
bullets.body: ARM is characterized as fitting every milestone on the enterprise AI timeline (2026+), with its architecture embedded in every NVIDIA GPU and AWS Graviton servers. The bull thesis frames ARM as the most foundational AI infrastructure play regardless of which model or hyperscaler wins.

bullets.title: AMZN: Iran claims IRGC launched cruise missiles at Amazon data infrastructure in Bahrain
bullets.body: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed to have launched cruise missiles targeting Amazon data infrastructure in Bahrain, per CNBC. The claim has not been officially confirmed; Bahrain reported air raid sirens and Kuwait reported responding to Iranian drones and missiles in the region. AWS runs significant Gulf infrastructure; unverified but warrants monitoring.

bullets.title: AAOI/LITE/AXTI: Photonics stocks defending support; sector consolidating at lows
bullets.body: Photonics sector is tightening at support: LITE bulls are defending lows with strong positioning; AXTI is in a wedge formation at its 200-day moving average; AAOI sellers appear exhausted around key support. LITE +9.25%, AXTI +14.12%, AAOI +15.6% on the session as part of the broader semi recovery.

bullets.title: NFLX: Stratechery analyzes Netflix earnings, questions whether company is 'washed'
bullets.body: Stratechery published an earnings analysis on Netflix questioning whether the company is losing momentum ('Is Netflix Washed?'). No specific price targets or directional calls extracted from the brief reference, but the piece is flagged as earnings-relevant commentary.

bullets.title: NOK: Earnings Thursday; first clean read on optical demand-supply dynamics
bullets.body: Nokia reports earnings Thursday; one analyst views it as the first direct read on demand-supply dynamics in the sector optics market, with AEHR providing only a partial signal. Author prefers entry at lower price levels and is seeking evidence of demand outrunning supply.
